title: Day 0 - Primer
headline: CODEBREAKER'S PRIMER
subheadline: Training cipher for new agents. Work the five tells in order: single-letter words, frequent letters, short words, apostrophes, then double letters. Tap a glyph and type — every copy of that glyph fills at once. For your first exercise, decode this standard training phrase designed to test your eye for common grammar patterns and identical consecutive characters.
originalText: I CAN'T SEE THE WORD THE AND LOOK AT A DOUBLE LETTER TOO.

title: Day 1 - Easy
headline: TRAGEDY AT THE VANCE ESTATE
subheadline: High society was rocked last night when Archibald Vance, the renowned railroad and shipping tycoon, was discovered deceased in his locked study during his annual gala. Thorne noted the absence of a weapon, yet a distinct, unnatural scent lingered in the stale air. A single crystal coupe glass sat perfectly centered on the mahogany desk, and a crumpled draft of a telegraph was recovered from Vance's tuxedo pocket. The medical examiner is baffled, but my gut says murder. What did the tycoon ingest, and what was he trying to send before his heart stopped? A closer look at the crystal coupe suggests the deadly concoction wasn't poured from the main bar, but slipped into a celebratory toast.
originalText: THE FATAL DOSE WAS IN THE CHAMPAGNE. THE TUXEDO TELEGRAPH.

title: Day 1 - Hard
headline: THE TUXEDO TELEGRAPH
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The paper found in Vance's pocket was recovered from the wire room after deadline. It proves the old man wasn't just sipping drinks—he was going to war. The late-city transmission is still in cipher. The decoded wire reveals Archibald's final, desperate promise to tear down his own empire by shining a light on his partners' sins.
originalText: HE THREATENED TO EXPOSE US ALL. THE WIDOW'S LAMENT.

title: Day 2 - Easy
headline: THE WIDOW'S LAMENT
subheadline: I interviewed Beatrice Vance this morning. The grieving widow was dressed in immaculate black silk, her eyes dry and her demeanor as cold as ice. She claims she was dancing with her husband's business partner at the exact time of the murder. But the upstairs maid confided in me that Beatrice and Archibald had a vicious, hushed argument just hours before the guests arrived. I found a charred scrap of heavy parchment near the fireplace in Beatrice's boudoir. It seems the flames didn't quite finish their job hiding her secrets. The heavy, watermarked paper bears the distinct seal of a law office, suggesting the flames were meant to consume a newly altered legal testament.
originalText: HE CHANGED THE WILL BEFORE THE GALA. THE SCORCHED FRAME.

title: Day 2 - Hard
headline: THE SCORCHED FRAME
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — Following the burned fragment's lead, detectives forced the library at dusk. The scrap points to a specific fixture in the room, but the precise hiding spot has not been typeset. The burnt scrap specifically directs our attention toward a piece of nautical decor that might be hiding a secret compartment.
originalText: LOOK BEHIND THE RED SAILBOAT. A MISSING HEIR.

title: Day 3 - Easy
headline: A MISSING HEIR
subheadline: Whispers echo through the hallowed halls of the Vance estate today following the reading of the late millionaire’s will. The lawyer revealed a shocking twist regarding the bulk of the massive fortune. The room erupted into chaos, and Arthur Sterling abruptly left the premises looking as pale as a man who had just seen a ghost. Our sources indicate a frantic search is underway. The police intercepted an unsigned postcard today, bearing a typed address to Sterling's office and a block of garbled text. It seems to be a desperate update sent to Sterling’s office from a shadow on the payroll. Rumors have long circulated about a young female ward hidden away from the public eye, and this garbled text might just confirm her fate.
originalText: THE GIRL IS STILL BREATHING. THE ALBANY STUB.

title: Day 3 - Hard
headline: THE ALBANY STUB
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The sun has set on the will reading. Sterling is not answering his door, but a night clerk at Grand Central sold the precinct a piece of paper recovered after the last train rolled out. This late dispatch is still in cipher. The scrap appears to be a transit receipt, confirming someone was quietly shipped north on a clandestine rail line.
originalText: BOUGHT HER A ONE WAY TICKET UPSTATE. SHADOWS IN THE OFFICE.

title: Day 4 - Easy
headline: SHADOWS IN THE OFFICE
subheadline: A midnight call roused me from what little slumber I had managed since the gala. A crew in Sterling’s pay broke into the Vance & Sterling Shipping Co. downtown. Curiously, they weren't after cash—the company safe was untouched. Instead, specific filing cabinets were stripped to the wood. Whatever Sterling is hiding, it involves the ghosts of the past. On the floor beneath the shattered window, I found a train ticket stub to Albany with a hastily scrawled coded message on the back—a directive from the men who scrubbed the files. The missing folders specifically held the company's maritime shipping manifests dating back exactly three years.
originalText: HIDING THE NINETEEN TWENTY THREE VOYAGES. THE EMPTIED CABINETS.

title: Day 4 - Hard
headline: THE EMPTIED CABINETS
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — Harbor watchmen swear The Midnight Runner takes on unmarked crates after the lights go out. A second cipher from the emptied logs has not been typeset. The cipher hints that the so-called textile shipments from Havana were actually a clever front for highly profitable, sloshy contraband.
originalText: THE CUBAN SILK IS LIQUID GOLD. AN INTERCEPTED WIRE.

title: Day 5 - Easy
headline: AN INTERCEPTED WIRE
subheadline: A stroke of luck. Our boys down at the telegraph office intercepted a message sent by Arthur Sterling to a mysterious "Mr. Black" at a private club in Albany. Sterling has been sweating bullets since the will reading, pacing his study until all hours. Beatrice Vance has also been seen entering Sterling’s estate through the servant's entrance. The telegraph operator managed to copy down two segments of the transmission before the line was suspiciously cut. In the first segment, Beatrice drops the grieving widow act and issues a hostile, frantic demand to Sterling. We must decode the rest immediately to intercept the courier. The fragment catches the widow demanding her cut of the illicit profits be delivered immediately to a high-end Manhattan hotel.
originalText: SEND MY HALF TO THE PLAZA. THE DEAD WIRE.
solvedInsert: CUT OUT RIGHT AFTER SHE TYPED

title: Day 5 - Hard
headline: THE DEAD WIRE
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — A second transmission was cut off when the line went dead at 11:47 p.m. Decode this night extra before the sender vanishes. The final, desperate strokes on the wire suggest a blackmail threat over unpaid medical bills, threatening to let their secret patient go free.
originalText: PAY THE CLINIC OR SHE WALKS. THE DOCTOR'S SECRET.
solvedInsert: WAS THAT HE WAS TOLD TO

title: Day 6 - Easy
headline: THE DOCTOR'S SECRET
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 9, 1926)
Three days on nothing but black coffee, Lucky Strikes, and a sleeping car to Albany. I stumbled off the platform in a rumpled suit, eyes bloodshot, following the ticket stub trail to the Blackwood Sanatorium. The head physician, Dr. Aris Blackwood, was remarkably uncooperative, insisting patient records were confidential and that Clara was resting securely in the west wing. His desk was littered with Beatrice’s perfumed letters. However, a sympathetic nurse slipped me a folded napkin as I left the grounds. It seems Dr. Blackwood is lying through his teeth to keep his monthly payments from Vance & Sterling Shipping Co. rolling in. The nurse’s frantic note contained a coded message detailing a sudden, massive problem at the facility. The nurse's hastily scribbled code warns that the doctor's prized patient is no longer confined to her room.
originalText: THE BIRD FLEW THE COOP ON SUNDAY. THE HOTEL NAPKIN.

title: Day 6 - Hard
headline: THE HOTEL NAPKIN
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — After dark, the sympathetic nurse slipped a second item under Detective Thorne’s hotel door: a torn, encoded page from the doctor’s personal ledger. The accounting lines expose a steady supply of heavy narcotics, authorized straight from the top to keep their captive docile.
originalText: HEAVY DOSES OF MORPHINE ORDERED BY STERLING. THE MIDNIGHT RUNNER.

title: Day 7 - Easy
headline: THE MIDNIGHT RUNNER
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The Waterfront Whisperer, Sept 10, 1926)
A suspicious vessel, The Midnight Runner, was raided by the Coast Guard late last night after attempting to slip past the federal blockade at Rum Row. Registered to Vance & Sterling Shipping Co., the cargo manifest claimed it was transporting textiles from Cuba. However, underneath the crates of silk, Volstead Act enforcers uncovered illicit cargo that had nothing to do with textiles. Witnesses say Detective Elias Thorne, still in yesterday’s rumpled suit and looking as though he had not slept since Albany, was already on the pier when the boarding party went over the rail. Dockhands swore they rarely saw Archibald down at the piers. There was a shadow broker calling the shots after sundown, a man who treated the fleet like his own personal toy. Was Archibald murdered to protect a million-dollar bootlegging empire from its rightful owner? A cryptic ledger was found in the captain’s quarters, containing an encoded entry that finally puts a name to the boss. The decoded text strips away the shadows, explicitly naming the surviving partner who now commands the entire smuggling fleet.
originalText: ARTHUR GIVES THE ORDERS NOW. THE CAPTAIN'S LEDGER.

title: Day 7 - Hard
headline: THE CAPTAIN'S LEDGER
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — Coast Guard papers seized from The Midnight Runner include a second ledger page the morning edition did not print, revealing exactly what triggered the tycoon's murder. This final entry documents the exact, fatal moment the late tycoon stumbled upon the illicit accounting that cost him his life.
originalText: THE OLD MAN FOUND THE RUM RUNNING BOOKS. THE BUTLER'S CONFESSION.

title: Day 8 - Easy
headline: THE BUTLER'S CONFESSION
subheadline:
(Police Interrogation Transcript - Sept 11, 1926)
I brought Reginald, the Vance family butler, in for questioning today. He has served the family for twenty years but looked as though he had aged a decade overnight. He finally broke under pressure, admitting he used his master key on the locked study minutes before Archibald Vance was found dead. As the oak door swung in, he caught a scent that was wildly out of place in a tycoon's cigar-smoke-filled sanctuary. When asked who rushed past him in the hall, Reginald clammed up, terrified for his life. A search of his quarters turned up a matchbook from a notorious downtown speakeasy, The Blind Tiger, with two messages scrawled inside. The first hasty scrawl on the matchbook cover reveals the shocking gender of the mysterious figure fleeing the scene of the crime.
originalText: A WOMAN WAS IN THE LOCKED STUDY. THE SECOND CONFESSION.

title: Day 8 - Hard
headline: THE SECOND CONFESSION
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — Under lamplight at headquarters the butler recanted part of his story and whispered a longer cipher. This whispered admission finally explains why the servant kept quiet, detailing a hefty cash bribe from a desperate medical man.
originalText: THE DOCTOR PAID ME FIFTY BUCKS TO TURN A BLIND EYE. SECRETS IN THE SAFE.

title: Day 9 - Easy
headline: SECRETS IN THE SAFE
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 12, 1926)
Using the lead decoded from the charred scrap, I located the hidden wall safe behind the library canvas. Inside lay an explosive cache of personal extortion files and a sealed document from twenty-four years ago stamped by city records, alongside a drafted hit-list proving the old man knew about the assassination plot and was preparing to strike first. I summoned Beatrice to the library and laid the contents on the mahogany desk. She went white as a sheet. What Archibald locked away wasn't just corporate corruption—it was the lie at the center of his family. The decades-old city record strips away the family's pristine image, exposing a scandalous, hidden truth about the missing heiress's real maternity.
originalText: THE WIDOW IS HER TRUE BIOLOGICAL MOTHER. THE MIDNIGHT INVENTORY.

title: Day 9 - Hard
headline: THE MIDNIGHT INVENTORY
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — A midnight inventory of the wall safe produced a second encoded letter in Clara’s hand. The morning paper held this dispatch back. This hidden letter captures the young woman's absolute fury, outlining a devastating promise to publicly ruin the matriarch who abandoned her.
originalText: CLARA VOWED TO EXPOSE HER OWN MOTHER. A VOICE FROM THE SHADOWS.

title: Day 10 - Easy
headline: A VOICE FROM THE SHADOWS
subheadline:
(Intercepted Letter - Sept 13, 1926)
A letter arrived at the precinct today, addressed directly to me. It smelled faintly of lavender and damp earth. The handwriting was elegant but frantic. It was from Clara Vance. She reveals she is hiding in plain sight in the city, terrified for her life. She claims her father’s death was just the beginning, and that The Blind Tiger is the center of the conspiracy. She watched from a priest-hole behind the bookshelves, but the angle was cruel: she could see only hands, hear a deep voice, and observe one highly distinctive accessory resting against the oak floorboards. The sanatorium narcotics have left her memory in fragments. The man’s face is a blur. She enclosed two ciphers, promising they hold the key to the killer's identity. Across the bottom she scrawled a desperate directive: track down the object mentioned in the code. The cipher explicitly describes this crucial floorboard accessory, pointing squarely to a suspect who requires ornate, metallic assistance to walk.
originalText: THE KILLER LEANS ON CARVED SILVER. THE SECOND LETTER.

title: Day 10 - Hard
headline: THE SECOND LETTER
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — A second letter arrived after dusk. Clara still cannot name the man with the deep voice. This night extra is the rest of her hand. However, she saw enough to know exactly how the poison breached the estate, pinning the smuggling operation directly on the grieving widow.
originalText: BEATRICE BROUGHT THE WEAPON INSIDE. INTO THE TIGER'S DEN.

title: Day 11 - Easy
headline: INTO THE TIGER'S DEN
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 14, 1926)
Following the matchbook clue, I traded my detective's coat for a cheap suit and slinked into The Blind Tiger. The speakeasy was thick with cigar smoke, bathtub gin, and the frantic rhythm of a ragtime band. Through the haze, I spotted Arthur Sterling tucked away in a velvet VIP booth, sweating profusely while whispering with some unfamiliar men who didn't look like shipping magnates. The bartender was acting as their go-between, passing folded notes under cocktail napkins. I swiped one of those napkins during a scuffle. The criminal underground is embedded in Vance's empire, and this cipher details exactly what Sterling is shopping for. The hurried handwriting confirms Sterling isn't just securing his shipping routes—he's actively purchasing brutal, hired thuggery from a notorious local gang.
originalText: BUYING MUSCLE FROM THE EAST SIDE BOYS. THE NAPKIN RING.

title: Day 11 - Hard
headline: THE NAPKIN RING
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — After closing time, a sweep of Sterling's booth yielded a crumpled slip from one of his inside men. It proves Sterling knows exactly how the killers breached the study. The crumpled note outlines the exact assassination method, confirming a gentleman's mobility aid was repurposed as a deadly, covert vessel.
originalText: THE DEADLY DOSE WAS SMUGGLED IN A WALKING STICK. THE HOLLOW CANE.

title: Day 12 - Easy
headline: THE HOLLOW CANE
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The New York Chronicle, Sept 15, 1926)
A major breakthrough in the Vance murder case! Spurred by the precinct's published reward notice, a local pawnshop owner stepped forward this morning with a silver-handled cane matching our description. The owner claims a woman draped in black veils pawned the item for a fraction of its worth just hours after the murder. Upon police inspection, the cane was abnormally heavy, its shaft hollowed out. I am submitting the item to the precinct lab, while I decode the pawn ticket left with it to verify my darkest suspicions. The pawn ticket's code hints at the cane's true, illicit engineering, confirming it was custom-built to hold a fatal liquid payload.
originalText: THE WALKING STICK WAS A CONCEALED FLASK. THE CHEMIST'S BENCH.

title: Day 12 - Hard
headline: THE CHEMIST'S BENCH
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — The laboratory lamps are still burning. The precinct chemists sent up their preliminary findings in a coded internal wire. We finally know what was inside. The decoded lab report identifies a telltale, distinctively nutty aroma clinging to the interior glass, a classic hallmark of a notorious and lethal poison.
originalText: TRACES OF BITTER ALMONDS IN THE GLASS TUBE. AN EMPTY ROOM.
solvedInsert: WAS ALL I FOUND AFTER DISCOVERING

title: Day 13 - Easy
headline: AN EMPTY ROOM
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 16, 1926)
Using the postmarks from Clara's letter, I tracked her hideout to a run-down boarding house in the Bowery. I was too late. The door hung off its hinges, and the small room had been violently tossed. A shattered mirror and a knocked-over chair pointed to a desperate struggle. Clara Vance has been taken. On the remaining shards of the vanity mirror, Clara had scrawled a preemptive warning in red lipstick before the door was breached. The letters were smudged, but I could read the grim realization of her capture. The smudged red letters perfectly capture her terrifying realization that the syndicate's relentless bloodhounds had finally tracked her down.
originalText: THE DOGS CAUGHT MY SCENT. THE LIPSTICK GLASS.

title: Day 13 - Hard
headline: THE LIPSTICK GLASS
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — Clara’s boarding-house room was empty by moonrise, but she left a longer warning than the lipstick on the glass. If her intel is good, the rot in this town doesn't stop at the docks—it climbs the marble steps. This late dispatch is still in cipher. This sinister cipher confirms that her kidnapping wasn't just a mob hit, but an operation officially sanctioned by the highest levels of municipal government.
originalText: CITY HALL SIGNED THE WARRANT FOR HER ABDUCTION. A GRUESOME DISCOVERY.

title: Day 14 - Easy
headline: A GRUESOME DISCOVERY
subheadline:
(Police Evidence File - September 17, 1926)
A body was pulled from the East River at dawn. My stomach dropped, fearing it was Clara, but the victim was identified as Reginald, the Vance family butler. His pockets had been violently turned inside out before the water took him, but his stiff fingers still clutched a shredded piece of Cuban silk. Attached to his suspenders was a waterproof oilskin pouch containing a torn page from Archibald Vance’s private ledger. Reginald swiped it before the cops arrived. But Reginald didn't write the cipher scrawled across the back in grease pencil—his killers did, leaving a grim epitaph for the precinct to find. The killers' crude handwriting mocks their victim's demands for a payoff, boasting about sending the blackmailing servant to a watery grave.
originalText: THE GREEDY SNITCH SANK TO THE BOTTOM OF THE RIVER. THE STUDY LEDGER.

title: Day 14 - Hard
headline: THE STUDY LEDGER
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — A second page from Archibald’s private study ledger, withheld from the morning run, is the missing inventory. The decoded inventory proves Archibald wasn't just moving illegal liquor, but was secretly arming the underworld with heavy, smuggled artillery.
originalText: GUNS HIDDEN BENEATH THE WHISKEY CRATES. THE MAYOR STEPS DOWN.

title: Day 15 - Easy
headline: THE MAYOR STEPS DOWN
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The Long Island Tattler, Sept 18, 1926)
In a shocking morning press conference, Mayor H. Harrison announced his immediate resignation, citing "sudden and severe health reasons." The city is buzzing with speculation, but our precinct knows the truth. Detective Thorne raided the Mayor’s private office just as the movers were packing his mahogany desk. Hidden in the false bottom of a cigar humidor, Thorne discovered a hidden file Archibald had been keeping on the Mayor’s inner circle. The Mayor’s pristine public image was a house of cards propped up by Tammany Hall fixers, and Vance owned the wind. Thorne has submitted two coded notes found clipped to the Mayor's file to the lab for decryption—messages that reveal the brutal dynamic between the two men. The first decrypted scrap details the sheer extent of Vance's leverage, proving the Mayor was little more than a puppet under the tycoon's total control.
originalText: THE TYCOON HELD THE POLITICIAN BY THE THROAT. THE HUMIDOR FILE.

title: Day 15 - Hard
headline: THE HUMIDOR FILE
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — After dark, a second threat arrived from the same blackmail file. This late-city cipher has not been typeset. This night dispatch shifts the crosshairs from municipal hall straight to precinct headquarters, exposing the top lawman's dirty share of the bootlegging pie.
originalText: THE TOP COP TAKES A CUT OF THE SMUGGLING. THE CHIEF'S DILEMMA.

title: Day 16 - Easy
headline: THE CHIEF'S DILEMMA
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 19, 1926)
With the Mayor stepping down and the Police Chief implicated in the blackmail ring, I realize I cannot trust my own department. I am entirely on my own. Last night, I broke into the Chief’s private office, searching for any indication of where Clara Vance might have been taken. Under his blotter, I discovered a carbon copy of a secretly intercepted telegraph message, routed away from my desk. It contained orders routing a heavily armed strike team, and a ticking clock. We must decode it before the hour runs out. The decrypted heading lays bare the tragic scope of the corruption, confirming that every officer on that strike team is answering to private payrolls.
originalText: THE BADGES ARE BOUGHT AND PAID FOR. THE CHIEF'S BLOTTER.

title: Day 16 - Hard
headline: THE CHIEF'S BLOTTER
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — A night courier brought the rest of the blotter orders. The clock is still running. This extra may be her last chance. The second half of the blotter orders lays out the grim deadline and exact waterfront location where the hit squad plans to silence Clara forever.
originalText: THE EXECUTION IS SCHEDULED FOR MIDNIGHT AT PIER FORTY FOUR. SHOOTOUT AT PIER 44.

title: Day 17 - Easy
headline: SHOOTOUT AT PIER 44
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The Waterfront Whisperer, Sept 20, 1926)
Gunfire shattered the midnight quiet at Pier 44! Battered by the torrential outer squalls of the hurricane currently devastating the Florida coast, the harbor was dark, flooded, and chaotic. A lone, rogue detective survived a fierce ambush on the wet timber. When the powder smoke lifted in the mist, the leader of the strike team went down hard, and the remaining badges had fled into the night, leaving behind a terrified but unharmed Clara Vance. The missing heiress has finally been found! Thorne escorted her to a secure, undisclosed location. There is no going back to the force now. Rumors say Clara has agreed to testify about the night of her father's murder, and what she witnessed from the secret passage in his study changes the entire investigation. She carried two coded notes she stole from her captors. The stolen note paints a dark picture of the aftermath, commemorating the corrupt officer who met his violent end on the rain-soaked planks.
originalText: A CROOKED STAR LEFT BLEEDING ON THE DOCKS. THE WAREHOUSE FLOOR.

title: Day 17 - Hard
headline: THE WAREHOUSE FLOOR
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The shootout left a second statement on the warehouse floor. Clara stole it from her captors. The second stolen paper exonerates one key suspect from the immediate crime scene, upending our timeline of who actually pulled the trigger.
originalText: ARTHUR NEVER STEPPED FOOT IN THE STUDY. THE DAUGHTER'S TALE.

title: Day 18 - Easy
headline: THE DAUGHTER'S TALE
subheadline:
(Police Interrogation Transcript - Sept 21, 1926)
Clara sat trembling, gripping a cold cup of black coffee. "The priest-hole gives you ears, Detective, but only slivers of sight," she whispered. "My father locked the heavy oak doors from within—he thought the deadbolt would keep him safe while he burned the shipping books. Then I heard footsteps in the hall, the distinct click of Reginald’s master key turning from the outside, followed by the heavy deadbolt sliding shut." For a second her trembling was replaced by a cold, familiar Vance smile. Then Clara broke down, unable to speak the names aloud, but she hastily sketched two ciphers detailing how the killers sealed themselves inside the horrific scene she witnessed. Her sketch underscores the chilling reality that two vicious conspirators trapped themselves in the dark room alongside their helpless victim.
originalText: A PAIR OF WOLVES LOCKED FROM THE INSIDE. THE PRIEST-HOLE.

title: Day 18 - Hard
headline: THE PRIEST-HOLE
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — After dusk Clara dictated a longer cipher. This night extra is the rest of what she could swear to. This night extra zeroes in on the voice Clara heard behind the wall, describing a chilling, professional cadence that points to a trained medical practitioner.
originalText: THE SHADOW SPOKE WITH A CLINICAL TONE. THE DOCTOR RETURNS.

title: Day 19 - Easy
headline: THE DOCTOR RETURNS
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 22, 1926)
A deep voice. A carved silver cane. A shadow Clara could not name. I brought in an abandoned leather kit recovered from a Grand Central locker and popped the latches. The sharp stench of sanatorium narcotics hit the room instantly, alongside a frantic, handwritten note: "I secured the cyanide, Bea. We take his money tonight." Clara’s hands began to shake violently—the sensory shock tore straight through her drug haze. "That smell... that voice in the study." Someone traveled hundreds of miles on gala night under an assumed name. The decoded evidence turns the asylum director's unexpected trip into a deadly house call, cementing his physical presence at the murder scene.
originalText: THE PHYSICIAN MADE A HOUSECALL FOR MURDER. THE MEDICAL BAG.

title: Day 19 - Hard
headline: THE MEDICAL BAG
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — A night search of the medical bag produced a second cipher revealing exactly what the doctor brought to the gala. This second cipher specifies the exact fatal compound the physician smuggled into the mansion to fuel his lover's deadly scheme.
originalText: HE SUPPLIED THE CYANIDE FOR HER PLOT. LOVERS ON THE RUN.

title: Day 20 - Easy
headline: LOVERS ON THE RUN
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The New York Chronicle, Sept 23, 1926)
A city-wide manhunt is underway for socialite Beatrice Vance and Dr. Aris Blackwood. Most of the city was glued to the radio broadcast of the Dempsey-Tunney heavyweight bout last night, leaving the streets practically deserted. Detective Thorne used the distraction to breach Beatrice's Plaza Hotel suite, only to find the wall safe emptied. A terrified maid reported seeing the pair fleeing toward the harbor, noting the doctor looked pale and frantic while Beatrice stared at him with cold, predatory eyes. The murderous lovers have made their escape, but a discarded telegraph draft in their wastebasket reveals their desperate destination. The recovered telegraph draft outlines the pair's escape vector, revealing their flight route toward warmer, unpoliced waters.
originalText: THE GUILTY BIRDS ARE FLYING SOUTH. THE LEATHER TRUNK.

title: Day 20 - Hard
headline: THE LEATHER TRUNK
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — Harbor pilots report a steamer clearing with a leather trunk in the hold. Decode the night extra before it clears the Hook. This harbor extra reveals a cunning misdirection by the fugitive couple, confirming the ship is nothing more than a decoy to throw off the search.
originalText: THE MURDERERS ARE NOT ON THAT BOAT. THE BAIT IS SET.

title: Day 21 - Easy
headline: THE BAIT IS SET
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 24, 1926)
With the local police force hopelessly compromised—and my own Chief dead by my hand at Pier 44—Clara and I cannot simply walk into a precinct. We need the rats to eat each other. I leaked two rumors through a trusted dockworker. One of them concerns a massive, unguarded payday moving through Pier 84. They will both come armed, each expecting to collect. We chose Pier 84 for the trap. A midnight rendezvous has been staged by a single lantern. I only hope their greed outweighs their caution. I dispatched my dockyard contacts to spread the bait. They just routed back an encoded confirmation that the trap is sprung. The dockworker's confirmation highlights the promise of fake fortune used to draw the conspirators out from hiding into the dark.
originalText: LURE THEM INTO THE OPEN WITH PHANTOM GOLD. THE SECOND RUMOR.

title: Day 21 - Hard
headline: THE SECOND RUMOR
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — A second courier slip went out after the morning rumor. Decode this night dispatch before the lantern is lit. This late dispatch warns of the extreme force heading toward the pier, promising that the targets won't be coming quietly.
originalText: EXPECT HEAVY ARTILLERY IN THE FOG. A SHOCKING ARRIVAL.

title: Day 22 - Easy
headline: A SHOCKING ARRIVAL
subheadline:
(Police Evidence File - Narrative Account, Sept 25, 1926)
The trap at Pier 84 was set. Clara stood nervously by a single flickering lantern, clutching a decoy ledger. I was perched high above in the rusted iron rafters, my revolver drawn. A sleek black Packard silently rolled onto the damp wooden docks. The driver's door swung wide, but it wasn't Sterling who stepped into the lamplight. It was the widow, wrapped in mink, her silhouette cutting through the mist. In the passenger seat sat a shadowy figure who never moved. Beatrice laughed coldly into the fog as her hand emerged from her coat. She didn't come to negotiate. The decoded evidence confirms the widow's lethal intentions, proving she chose gunpowder over legal counsel to resolve the dispute.
originalText: THE WIDOW BROUGHT LEAD INSTEAD OF LAWYERS. THE PACKARD DOOR.

title: Day 22 - Hard
headline: THE PACKARD DOOR
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — When the smoke cleared over the Packard, detectives found Dr. Blackwood slumped in the front seat, his own gun drawn but unfired. The bullet didn't come from Sterling's mob or Thorne's revolver. The powder burns on the doctor's lapel told a far colder story. The close-range powder burns betray the ultimate act of betrayal, confirming Beatrice eliminated her lover to avoid splitting the fortune.
originalText: SHE SLAUGHTERED THE DOCTOR TO KEEP ALL THE LOOT. HONOR AMONG THIEVES.

title: Day 23 - Easy
headline: HONOR AMONG THIEVES
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 26, 1926)
Before Beatrice could pull the trigger, I dropped a flash flare from the rafters, allowing Clara to scramble behind heavy iron freight crates as the shadows around the Packard shifted. Arthur Sterling stepped forward with his hired guns, exactly as I had baited him. He knew someone was setting a trap, and as the two rival crews collided in the fog, Sterling smugly shifted his position, revealing a brutal tactical advantage to ensure his own survival. Mob enforcers and Beatrice’s remaining muscle melted out of the fog, surrounding the desperate pair, guns drawn. I stayed in the rafters and let the wolves work. A terrifying Mexican standoff ensued on the rotting planks of the pier. From high in the ironwork, Thorne witnesses the true depth of Sterling's cowardice as he drags Beatrice into harm's way as a physical barrier against the gunfire.
originalText: USING THE MOTHER AS A MEAT SHIELD. FROM THE RAFTERS.

title: Day 23 - Hard
headline: FROM THE RAFTERS
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — Honor among thieves lasted until moonrise. This cipher is what Thorne overheard from the rafters. The eavesdropped exchange reveals Sterling's hidden leverage, proving he held onto the fatal poison vial to control his co-conspirators.
originalText: ARTHUR KEPT THE CYANIDE FLASK FOR BLACKMAIL. AFTER THE BLOOD.

title: Day 24 - Easy
headline: AFTER THE BLOOD
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The New York Chronicle, Sept 27, 1926)
By the time the sirens reached Pier 84, the rival factions had already shredded one another in the harbor's gloom. Detective Thorne did not call his old precinct. He arranged the meeting so Sterling’s mob and Beatrice’s hired guns would do the killing for him, sitting in the rafters until the shooting slowed. Only then did his timed tip bring a different breed of authorities swarming over the docks to handle the gruesome aftermath. Beatrice Vance dropped what was left of her Derringer and wept for a lawyer. Arthur Sterling attempted to sprint toward a waiting speedboat, but Thorne finally came down from the iron and tackled him to the dock, sending his loaded revolver plunging into the dark waters of the Hudson River. The reign of the Vance & Sterling crime syndicate has violently ended. Thorne's calculated delay ensured federal agents arrived just in time to clear the dock floor and take over the crime scene.
originalText: LET THE FEDS SWEEP UP THE BODIES. THE TREASURY CLEANUP.
solvedInsert: BEGAN THE MOMENT WE DECIDED TO

title: Day 24 - Hard
headline: THE TREASURY CLEANUP
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — The harbor cleanup is not the last chapter. A final piece of paper fluttered from Sterling's coat during the struggle. This late cipher hints at a massive unresolved loose end. The dropped paper exposes a critical financial loose end, confirming that the syndicate's vast wealth remains hidden far from public view.
originalText: THE SYNDICATE ACCOUNTS ARE STILL BURIED. A CONFESSION UNDER NEON.

title: Day 25 - Easy
headline: A CONFESSION UNDER NEON
subheadline:
(Police Interrogation Transcript - Federal Bureau, Sept 28, 1926)
Sitting under the buzzing neon of the federal holding tank, Arthur Sterling finally cracked. With his dock muscle behind bars, the arrogance was gone. "I'm a bootlegger, not a butcher," he spat, pointing at the two-way glass. "I supplied the cane, but the widow poured the glass. The old man was locked in that study, and I was on the ballroom floor in plain view of fifty guests!" Clara watched through the two-way mirror as Sterling slid a feverish, encoded confession across the table, revealing exactly how the poison was administered. The bootlegger's signed statement pins the act directly on Beatrice, attesting that she personally laced and served her husband's final glass.
originalText: THE WIFE SERVED THE DEADLY VINTAGE. THE SECOND SIGNATURE.

title: Day 25 - Hard
headline: THE SECOND SIGNATURE
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — After the lights dimmed in the interrogation room he added a second cipher. Clara watched from behind the glass. This secondary admission legally seals the widow's mastermind role, cornering her into one final, desperate play.
originalText: A SIGNED CONFESSION PINS THE MASTERMIND. THE WIDOW'S LAST STAND.

title: Day 26 - Easy
headline: THE WIDOW'S LAST STAND
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The Waterfront Whisperer, Sept 29, 1926)
In federal custody, Beatrice Vance attempted one final, desperate play. She demanded a private meeting with the government's lead attorney, leaning in close to whisper a scandalous proposition, casually checking her reflection in the interrogation mirror while bargaining with a man's life. The prosecutor was unswayed. Detective Thorne bribed the court stenographer for a carbon copy of the transcript, which I’ve run through our precinct cipher desk to hide from prying eyes. The trial of the century begins tomorrow, and the city's corrupt elite are trembling as subpoenas are handed out like candy. The intercepted transcript details Beatrice's attempt to buy her freedom, offering her illicit fortune in exchange for dropped charges.
originalText: OFFERING BLOOD MONEY FOR CLEMENCY. THE VAULT INVENTORY.

title: Day 26 - Hard
headline: THE VAULT INVENTORY
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — A night inventory of the secured assets produced a shocking ledger. This final line is the one the morning paper would not print. The confidential audit drops a major bombshell regarding the true ownership of the syndicate's hidden offshore wealth.
originalText: THE OFFSHORE VAULT BELONGS TO THE DAUGHTER. THE TRIAL OF THE CENTURY.

title: Day 27 - Easy
headline: THE TRIAL OF THE CENTURY
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Sept 30, 1926)
The supreme court gallery was packed to the rafters as the joint capital murder trial of Arthur Sterling and Beatrice Vance commenced. Photographers' flashbulbs popped like firecrackers as Clara Vance took the witness stand. Dressed in a modest navy suit, she recounted her father’s murder and her harrowing abduction with a poise that captured the courtroom's sympathy instantly. Sterling’s high-priced attorneys attempted to poke holes in my rogue investigation, but the federal prosecutor introduced Exhibit A—Thorne's most damning piece of physical evidence recovered from the waterfront. The jury has the case. I am waiting in the gallery for the slip of paper that ends it. The prosecutor's critical evidence submission delivers the decisive blow, using recovered financial records to seal both defendants' fates.
originalText: THE BOOTLEGGING LEDGER SEALS THEIR FATE. THE PROSECUTOR'S SLIP.

title: Day 27 - Hard
headline: THE PROSECUTOR'S SLIP
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — The jury was out less than an hour. A second encoded note from the prosecutor’s table records what the morning extras could not wait for. The swift verdict hands down the ultimate penalty, clearing away legal obstacles and settling the fate of the Vance empire.
originalText: A GUILTY VERDICT DEMANDS THE ELECTRIC CHAIR. THE SECRET INHERITANCE.

title: Day 28 - Easy
headline: THE SECRET INHERITANCE
subheadline:
(Police Evidence File - Narrative Account, Oct 1, 1926)
With the jury deliberating Beatrice’s fate, Clara returned to the quiet estate escorted by Detective Thorne. Waiting in the study was Archibald's private attorney, holding a brass lockbox stamped with instructions to open only upon Vance's unnatural death. Beatrice spent months conspiring to murder her husband for control of the shipping line, but Archibald had anticipated the wolves at his throat long before the night of the gala. Inside the box rested a single coded directive in the tycoon's handwriting. Archibald's posthumous directive reveals he legally stripped Beatrice of her prize long before she ever struck.
originalText: THE PATENTS AND SHIPS WERE SIGNED OVER YEARS AGO. THE DEAD MAN'S HAND.

title: Day 28 - Hard
headline: THE DEAD MAN'S HAND
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — Among Archibald’s papers Thorne found a longer cipher in the dead man’s hand. This is his last night letter. The tycoon's final letter proves his demise was part of a calculated trap designed to dismantle his killers from beyond the grave.
originalText: THE OLD MAN ENGINEERED HIS OWN REVENGE. A NEW DAWN.

title: Day 29 - Easy
headline: A NEW DAWN
subheadline:
(Newspaper Clipping - The New York Chronicle, Oct 2, 1926)
A crisp autumn wind blew off the harbor as Clara Vance stood before the headquarters of the newly renamed Vance Maritime Company. Her first act as sole proprietor took place behind closed doors with the company ledgers. She worked through the night with a red pen, issuing a series of unyielding directives to sever the company's darkest ties. Detective Thorne watched from the docks as the reformed fleet departed the harbor. The rot looked cut out of New York. Thorne’s smile did not quite reach his eyes. There were still a few lines left in his journal. Her midnight reforms focus directly on the shipping paperwork, systematically erasing every criminal connection from the company manifests.
originalText: PURGING THE SYNDICATE FROM THE MANIFESTS. AFTER THE DOCKS WENT QUIET.

title: Day 29 - Hard
headline: AFTER THE DOCKS WENT QUIET
subheadline: NIGHT EXTRA — After the docks went quiet, Thorne watched Clara at her father’s old safe. Decode what he wrote down. Thorne's observation log notes that despite the safe being opened, certain dark family secrets will stay buried forever.
originalText: SOME SECRETS REMAIN BURIED IN THE MASTER STUDY. CASE CLOSED.

title: Day 30 - Easy
headline: CASE CLOSED
subheadline:
(Journal Entry - Detective Elias Thorne, Oct 3, 1926)
I sit in my favorite diner, watching the rain wash the city streets clean. I left my tarnished badge on the counter to pay for the coffee. The Vance case is officially closed. Arthur Sterling and Beatrice Vance sit in Sing Sing’s death cells awaiting the electric chair, and Mayor Harrison’s corrupt administration is nothing but a disgraced memory. After Pier 44, there is no precinct that would have me, and none I would have back. Before she left for a tour of Europe, Clara Vance sent me a small, heavy package containing a parting gift, and an envelope containing two final ciphers. The first note held a profound expression of gratitude for my protection. It’s a quiet morning. New York feels safer. I know better than to call it honest. The heavy package reveals a tangible token of gratitude, honoring the detective's sacrifices with a lasting, blood-stained keepsake.
originalText: A GOLD WATCH BOUGHT WITH BLOOD AND BRASS. CLARA'S LAST ENVELOPE.

title: Day 30 - Hard
headline: CLARA'S LAST ENVELOPE
subheadline: LATE CITY FINAL — The diner was quiet this morning. Clara’s last envelope, opened under the night lamps of the Chronicle composing room, contains a longer farewell. Her final written message offers a bittersweet sign-off, expressing profound appreciation for Thorne's crusade to cleanse the city.
originalText: THE CITY IS NEVER CLEAN DETECTIVE BUT YOU MADE IT BREATHE AGAIN.
